expansion:
Use case: precise-object-edit / expansion of an existing watercolor side-view platformer design. The supplied image is the visual identity and mechanism reference. RECONSTRUCT it as a substantially LONGER, MORE INTRICATE level, not merely adding identical stairs. Create ONE tall art-direction sheet with THREE wide landscape watercolor gameplay panoramas stacked vertically, narrow ivory gutters. Each panel is a consecutive side-on orthographic window into the SAME continuous underground garden drain. Match reference brushwork, fine dark ink platform contours, damp brick, old bronze, jade moss, golden light, roots and reflective blue shallow water. Quiet readable rear wall, detailed foreground. No isometric perspective. SAME tiny ivory big-head flame spirit, SAME scale in all three panels, about 1/30 panel width. Each panel can show one instance of the same spirit at its local action point, not multiple spirits in one panel. Clean concise Chinese captions only in the ivory gutters.
Level length now about 76 character heights, roughly 5 gameplay camera widths. The panels show overlapping world intervals A=0–30H, B=24–54H, C=48–78H. Recognizable overlapping masonry and root landmarks connect the windows, not three unrelated dungeons.
PANEL A caption: “A 开灯与过闸 · 中位搭路”
Left: modest dark brick entrance from the pot connector, shallow flooded gutter below dry broken ledges. A bronze pull lever opens a maintenance lantern shutter via a thin discreet wall cord. About six differently sized dry ledges / brick piers require easy but real jumps with flat tops, alternating low and medium elevations, NOT continuous stair steps. Toward RIGHT, a taller old sluice inspection shaft opens in the brick vault. At world x25H (about 83 percent panel width), an antique overhead lantern emits one vertical golden ray DOWN to a small 45-degree BACKSLASH reflector on a vertical guide carriage. The reflector is in a MIDDLE position. Its reflected ray points HORIZONTALLY RIGHT, exiting the panel, not toward the floor.
A counterweight step is suspended LEFT of the mirror shaft near x22.5H, a little mossy iron cradle with a flat standing surface. A clearly connected taut chain over two fixed overhead guide wheels joins counterweight and mirror carriage: mirror UP means counterweight DOWN. There are TWO small hand winches linked to the same drive shaft: lower accessible crank on left bank x20H, second crank on the right upper bank x29H. The middle position places the counterweight step between two otherwise-too-far-apart banks, forming two feasible short jumps. The spirit is standing near the left crank. Mirror carriage itself is NOT ridden. Mark the step with a subtle vertical double arrow, not a giant elevator cage. Preserve visible pulley, axle, ratchet and support logic.
PANEL B caption: “B 升镜与折返 · 高位送光”
Show same inspection shaft partially overlapping at FAR LEFT, with the same old lantern and mirror now in HIGH position. Mirror has risen, counterweight step is now lower, ropes still taut. One horizontal golden beam runs high across the panel above the playable route and through an ACTUAL small aperture in any intervening masonry rib; no beam through opaque stone. The spirit is by the upper crank, with a wide resting ledge beside it.
The route after the shaft has an elaborate two-tier broken maintenance gallery: staggered narrow brick caps, small stone cantilevers, sections of rusty grille and short root-bound planks. Include a compact SWITCHBACK climb around one broken wall pier: approach right on lower shelves, climb back left through two offset footholds, then continue right on an upper shelf. Upper/lower paths must be spaced to leave room for the little spirit; usable jump gaps roughly one character height; clear landings, no massive unjumpable chasms. Separate foreground walking shelves from quieter decorative rear arches. A small safe resting platform halfway through, with a warm moss patch. Bottom shallow-water return route and low recovery steps connect to the nearest resting platform. The vertical shaft is a locally taller maintenance well, not the whole garden enlarged.
PANEL C caption: “C 窄台与摆渡 · 连跳至光鳞”
Continue same high horizontal ray from LEFT to the RIGHT feeding scale. Far left repeats the final mossy buttress and hanging root knot from panel B as continuity landmark. This is the most challenging section: first three separated narrow flat-topped brick caps at ALTERNATING heights, then a broad resting ledge, then ONE small water-driven inspection platform moving SLOWLY horizontally on an old wall-mounted rail across a wider broken section. The moving platform is flat, about 1.3 character-heights wide, with a clearly visible short rail and restrained horizontal double arrow. Show ONE platform at its current position, not ghost copies; it is not another mirror. Water pressure / an old paddle linkage below makes its cyclic motion plausible. A fixed safe takeoff ledge and fixed landing ledge on either side. Then three short precise jumps through staggered stone brackets, followed by a WIDE final landing. No monotonous stair ramp. No spikes, lava, enemies, collectibles or UI.
At far right, only a small cropped soft ivory TAIL-ROOT skin patch with pearly scales emerges through old mortar; one almond-shaped golden feeding scale receives the horizontal beam. The rest of giant creature stays hidden; no complete animal or head. Its local skin fold lifts enough to uncover a small existing masonry outlet below. The spirit is on the safe ledge before the moving platform, same tiny scale as in A and B.
Keep some individual platforms narrower than the reference, but leave foot space. Main route about 24–28 jumps over the whole level. Use alternating landing heights, pauses, a switchback and counterweight logic for complexity, not huge distances. Return paths under each section are recovery loops and MUST NOT provide a continuous walk to the exit. No gigantic rocks. Preserve golden focal light and cool damp watercolor atmosphere. This is a readable three-panel level DESIGN proposal, showing a sequence of puzzle states: middle in A, high in B and C. No paragraphs of text inside scenery.
correction:
Make a tightly localized practical correction to this THREE-PANEL watercolor level-design sheet. Keep all three panels, captions, palette, character sizes, optical paths, camera, architecture and C panel unchanged.
PANEL A ONLY: The hanging counterweight step currently floats too high to jump onto. LOWER THIS SAME flat mossy iron cradle until its top is just 0.4–0.6 tiny-character heights ABOVE the tops of the immediately adjacent fixed brick piers on its left and right. It must actually bridge the big gap between those piers. In this 1024x1536 sheet, the cradle is roughly x483–579 y180–199; move it down to around y260–279, keeping its x and width. Extend BOTH vertical hanging chains to the lowered cradle and keep them connected to the same overhead wheels. Leave the right sloping MIRROR where it is, and keep its golden ray unchanged. Do not retain a ghost cradle at the old high position. Do not add new platforms, scaffolding or a giant elevator. This is the middle traversable setting.
PANEL B ONLY: The upper maintenance gallery currently includes an almost continuous little wood walkway/rail at the upper right. Make this a broken 2D PLATFORM-JUMP route: interrupt that wood/grille tread with three clearly visible short gaps, each about one tiny spirit height wide. The rear support railing can stay discreetly behind it, but must not appear to be another walkable continuous bridge. Keep broad safe ledges before and after the gap sequence, the lower return route and the blue root landmark at the far right. Do not change the lantern, high mirror, lowered counterweight or light beam. Preserve the central masonry beam aperture.
This is a targeted edit, no whole-sheet restyling, no new title text.
